correctness.rationale: For every d>=2, exact spherical-cap integration gives the regularized beta lens and its nonzero negative derivative; the Rogers–Shephard equality case gives the simplex profile. Brunn–Minkowski produces concavity, analyticity and strict increase of r_d(s)/(1-s), with endpoint ratios 1 and d*kappa_d/(2*kappa_{d-1})>c_d. This proves exactly one nontrivial root and both strict sign regions. The source spherical containment gives s_d>sigma_d. A uniform endpoint integration-by-parts bound and Stirling expansion lead to s_d=3/5-[7log(pi*d)+18log3-27log2]/(50d)+O(log^2(d)/d^2), with constant 2^(9/10)/(pi^(7/30)*3^(3/5)) for s_d^d. The 749-check verifier independently reproduces lens quadrature, derivative, root, finite strict margin and asymptotic, without substituting finite data for proof.

value.rationale: The active theta-convolution extremal problem needs precise obstructions to a simplex candidate. The exact all-dimensional ball-vs-simplex transition strictly improves the earlier sufficient ball exclusion threshold sigma_d for every d and quantifies the true crossover with a universal 3/5 exponential base and nontrivial d^(-7/30) correction. These exact thresholds cannot be inferred from the earlier loose ball inclusion and are mathematically useful even without identifying global minimizers.
